subject.title: Owner-signed responsibility gates for assistant memory, actions, skills, and evidence reuse

question: Should OpenClaw define owner-confirmed responsibility state as a core/plugin contract now, or keep this as external/plugin-level governance until narrower memory provenance and action-gate issues land?
rationale: The request is valid security design work, but implementing it requires product and security choices across memory persistence, plugin SDK contracts, approval semantics, UI/audit state, and public config that automation should not decide.

options.title: Keep as design umbrella
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella and split implementation into narrower maintainer-approved memory, action, skill, and evidence lifecycle contracts.

options.title: Route to plugin first
options.body: Ask contributors to prototype the lifecycle as a plugin or ClawHub package and only add core/plugin API seams that the prototype proves are missing.

options.title: Decline core lifecycle
options.body: Close this direction as out of core scope and rely on existing approvals, Skill Workshop, memory guidance, and external responsibility-chain tools.

recommendation.title: Keep as design umbrella
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella and split implementation into narrower maintainer-approved memory, action, skill, and evidence lifecycle contracts.

likelyOwner.reason: The memory host SDK history and VISION-aligned core/plugin boundary make this the best available routing candidate among the observed contributors.
